title: AGROVOC Multilingual Thesaurus
description: AGROVOC is FAO's multilingual controlled vocabulary for agriculture, food, nutrition, fisheries, forestry, environment and related domains. The 2026-11-05 release has 42,100 concepts and 1,266,017 lexical labels in 42 languages (10.2 million triples), published as SKOS with SKOS-XL reified labels. Concepts are linked by SKOS hierarchical, associative and mapping relations (exactMatch and closeMatch to other thesauri) and by the Agrontology, FAO's ontology of domain relations (hasPest, isProducedBy, hasTaxonomicRank, ...). In Smart Data Models terms, AGROVOC is the reference vocabulary that agrifood entities can point to, e.g. the crop of an AgriParcel or the species of an Animal.
publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), with the AGROVOC editorial community

models.name: Concept
models.title: Smart Data Models - AGROVOC - Concept
models.description: An idea or notion; a unit of thought (skos:Concept). In AGROVOC, one of about 42,100 concepts covering agriculture, food, nutrition, fisheries, forestry, environment and related domains, labelled in up to 42 languages and linked by SKOS hierarchical/associative relations, mappings to other vocabularies, and the Agrontology's specific relations (e.g. hasPest, isProducedBy, hasTaxonomicRank). Attributes are the properties actually used on AGROVOC concepts in release 2026-11-05 (counted on the AGROVOC SPARQL endpoint), named exactly as in SKOS, SKOS-XL, DCMI and the Agrontology.

models.name: ConceptScheme
models.title: Smart Data Models - AGROVOC - ConceptScheme
models.description: A set of concepts, optionally including statements about semantic relationships between them (skos:ConceptScheme). Here, the AGROVOC thesaurus itself and its top concepts. Attributes are the properties actually used on AGROVOC concept schemes in release 2026-11-05 (counted on the AGROVOC SPARQL endpoint), named exactly as in SKOS, SKOS-XL, DCMI and the Agrontology.

models.name: Label
models.title: Smart Data Models - AGROVOC - Label
models.description: A reified lexical label (skosxl:Label). AGROVOC publishes every preferred, alternative and hidden label as its own resource with an AgrovocCode notation, a term type and term-to-term relations (acronyms, synonyms, scientific names, old names, symbols). Attributes are the properties actually used on AGROVOC labels in release 2026-11-05 (counted on the AGROVOC SPARQL endpoint), named exactly as in SKOS, SKOS-XL, DCMI and the Agrontology.

title: Battery Pass Data Model
description: Data model for the EU battery passport required by the Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, developed by the Battery Pass consortium and aligned with DIN DKE SPEC 99100 ("Requirements for data attributes of the battery passport"). It is split into seven SAMM aspect models: general product information, carbon footprint, circularity (dismantling, spare parts, recycled and renewable content, safety, end of life), labels and declaration of conformity, material composition (chemistry, critical raw materials, hazardous substances), performance and durability (rated technical properties and the dynamic battery condition, i.e. state of health), and supply chain due diligence.

title: Beneficial Ownership Data Standard (BODS)
description: The Beneficial Ownership Data Standard (BODS), published by Open Ownership, is the open standard for publishing information about who ultimately owns and controls companies and other legal entities and arrangements. Data is a series of Statements, each a claim made at a point in time about a record: an entity (company, trust, state body, ...), a natural person, or a relationship (the interests, such as shareholdings, voting rights or board appointment, that an interested party holds in an entity). It is used by beneficial ownership registers, public procurement and anti-corruption programmes, and by the Open Ownership Register.
publisher: Open Ownership

models.name: EntityStatement

models.description: Statement. A claim about a person, entity or relationship, made at a particular point in time. Beneficial Ownership Data Standard 0.4.0, https://standard.openownership.org/en/0.4.0/_static/entity-record.json. The Statement fields and the recordDetails fields are attributes of the entity; names are kept verbatim except 'source' -> 'bodsSource'.

title: Brick Schema
description: Uniform metadata schema for buildings: a vocabulary for describing the points (sensors, setpoints, commands, statuses, alarms), equipment (AHUs, chillers, pumps, VAVs, network devices, etc.), and their relationships (hasPoint/isPointOf, hasPart/isPartOf, feeds/isFedBy, hasUnit via QUDT) in building automation and IoT deployments. Widely used in the building controls / smart buildings community.
publisher: Brick Consortium (UC Berkeley, with industry and academic contributors); ontology hosted at ontology.brickschema.org

models.name: CO2_Level_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - CO2_Level_Sensor
models.description: Measures the concentration of CO2 in air (brick:CO2_Level_Sensor's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology). A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:CO2_Level_Sensor, hierarchy: CO2_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: Collection
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Collection
models.description: A logical grouping of points, equipment or other entities that doesn't correspond to a physical or system relationship (brick:Collection and its subclasses, e.g. Automation_Collection). INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN: Collection has no Brick-native membership property in any real Brick example checked (examples/collection/collection.ttl, examples/chiller-system/chiller-plant.ttl, examples/iaq_sensor_deployment) -- every real Collection instance found expresses its membership via RealEstateCore's rec:includes / rec:hasMember, not a Brick property. One of Brick's own example files even comments on this directly. This schema is therefore published as a placeholder (identity + brickClass only, no members) rather than either inventing a non-Brick property or silently omitting Collection altogether. A membership Relationship should be added once the planned RealEstateCore candidate exists for it to point to.

models.name: Equipment
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Equipment
models.description: A physical piece of equipment in a building's mechanical, electrical or IT systems: an air handling unit, chiller, pump, VAV box, thermostat, network device, etc. (brick:Equipment and its subclasses, Brick Schema). Modeled generically -- see the brickClass property -- rather than as hundreds of separate entity types.

models.name: Occupancy_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Occupancy_Sensor
models.description: Detects the presence or count of occupants. Unlike the other five classes in this batch, Occupancy_Sensor has no brick:hasSubstance in the source ontology (occupancy isn't a property of a substance/medium the way temperature or a gas concentration is) -- this schema therefore has no hasSubstance property at all, rather than an empty or null one. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Occupancy_Sensor, hierarchy: Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:PM10_Sensor, hierarchy: Particulate_Matter_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.description: A functional grouping of equipment that together provide a building service, e.g. an HVAC system or a chilled water system (brick:System and its subclasses). One of Brick's own example files even comments on this directly. This schema is therefore published as a placeholder (identity + brickClass only, no members) rather than either inventing a non-Brick property or silently omitting System altogether. A membership Relationship should be added once the planned RealEstateCore candidate exists for it to point to.

models.name: Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor
models.description: A temperature sensor for the air within an HVAC zone -- one specific member of Brick's broader Temperature_Sensor family (which also includes e.g. Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor, Discharge_Air_Temperature_Sensor). Modeled as its own class here because this is the exact leaf class in the real example data (a thermostat's zone sensor); the other family members share the same property shape and could be added the same way. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor, hierarchy: Air_Temperature_Sensor -> Temperature_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

title: Catena-X semantic models (Industry Core aspect models)
description: Catena-X is the automotive data space. Its semantic models are SAMM (Semantic Aspect Meta Model) aspect models: each one describes one aspect of a digital twin, and a twin is identified by its globalAssetId (formerly catenaXId). This candidate covers the Industry Core, the set of aspects that every Catena-X traceability use case builds on: the twin itself (SerialPart, Batch, JustInSequencePart for instances; PartType for part types) and the single-level relations between twins (bill of material and usage, as built and as planned).
publisher: Catena-X Automotive Network e.V., published through the Eclipse Tractus-X project (Eclipse Foundation)

models.name: Batch
models.title: Smart Data Models - Catena-X - Batch
models.description: A batch is a quantity of(semi-)finished products or(raw)material product that have been produced under the same circumstances(e.g. same production location), as specified groups or amounts, within a certain time frame. Every batch can differ in the number or amount of products. Different batches can have varied specifications, e.g., different colors. A batch is identified via a Batch ID. (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.batch:4.0.0#Batch, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.description: A just-in-sequence part is an instantiation of a (design-)part, where the particular instantiation can be uniquely identified by means of a combination of several IDs related to a just-in-sequence process. (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.just_in_sequence_part:4.0.0#JustInSequencePart, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.name: PartType
models.title: Smart Data Models - Catena-X - PartType
models.description: A Part Type represents an item in the Catena-X Bill of Material (BOM) on a type level in a specific version. (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.part_type:2.0.0#PartType, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.name: SerialPart
models.title: Smart Data Models - Catena-X - SerialPart
models.description: A serialized part is an instantiation of a (design-)part, where the particular instantiation can be uniquely identified by means of a serial number or a similar identifier (e.g. VAN)or a combination of multiple identifiers (e.g. combination of manufacturer, date and number) (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.serial_part:4.0.0#SerialPart, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.name: SingleLevelBomAsBuilt
models.title: Smart Data Models - Catena-X - SingleLevelBomAsBuilt
models.description:
The single-level bill of material represents one sub-level of an assembly and does not include any lower-level subassemblies. The as-built lifecycle references all child items as manufactured by the manufacturer referencing only child items in an as-built lifecycle themselves (e.g. serial parts or batches), unless parts can only be tracked by an part ID (on a type level).

If it is unclear which item has been built-in into the parent item, all potential parts must be listed. This is the case when, e.g. the same item is supplied by two suppliers and the item is only tracked by a customer part ID during assembly, these items can not be differentiated from each other. (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.single_level_bom_as_built:4.0.0#SingleLevelBomAsBuilt, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.name: SingleLevelBomAsPlanned
models.title: Smart Data Models - Catena-X - SingleLevelBomAsPlanned
models.description:
The single-level bill of material (BoM) represents one sub-level of an assembly and does not include any lower-level subassemblies. In the As-Planned lifecycle state all variants are covered ("120% BoM").
If multiple versions of child parts exist that can be assembled into the same parent part, all versions of the child part are included in the BoM.
If there are multiple suppliers for the same child part, each supplier has an entry for their child part in the BoM. (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.single_level_bom_as_planned:4.0.0#SingleLevelBomAsPlanned, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.name: SingleLevelUsageAsBuilt
models.title: Smart Data Models - Catena-X - SingleLevelUsageAsBuilt
models.description: The aspect provides the information in which parent part(s)/product(s)the given item is assembled in. Could be a 1:1 relationship in terms of an e.g. a brake component or 1:n for e.g. coatings. The parent item must refer to an object from as-built lifecycle phase, i.e. a batch or a serialized part. (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.single_level_usage_as_built:4.0.0#SingleLevelUsageAsBuilt, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.name: SingleLevelUsageAsPlanned
models.title: Smart Data Models - Catena-X - SingleLevelUsageAsPlanned
models.description:
The aspect provides the information in which parent part(s)/product(s)the given item is to be assembled into or used. This could be a 1:1 relationship in terms of a e.g. a brake component or 1:n for e.g. coatings. The given item as well as the parent item must refer to an object from the as-planned lifecycle phase.
If multiple versions of parent parts exist that the child part can be assembled into or used, all versions of the parent part are included in the usage list. (Catena-X aspect model urn:samm:io.catenax.industry_core.single_level_usage_as_planned:3.0.0#SingleLevelUsageAsPlanned, translated from the SAMM-generated JSON Schema; aspect property names and nested structures are kept verbatim.)

models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#BuildingRoom. An interior space (room) within a Building, bounded by walls/floor/ceiling. Part of the Building family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Building module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: BuildingStorey
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - BuildingStorey
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#BuildingStorey. A horizontal storey/floor of a Building, grouping the BuildingRooms on that level. Part of the Building family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Building module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: BuildingUnit
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - BuildingUnit
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#BuildingUnit. A functional/ownership unit of a Building, e.g. an apartment or office suite, which may span multiple BuildingRooms. Part of the Building family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Building module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: CityFurniture
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - CityFurniture
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#CityFurniture. Street furniture and small urban objects not part of a Building/Bridge/Tunnel, e.g. street lights, benches, traffic signs. Generic / unclassified City Object. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Generic module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: CityObjectGroup
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - CityObjectGroup
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#CityObjectGroup. A group of City Objects referenced as `children` (with optional `children_roles` describing each member's role in the group), e.g. a building complex or an aggregation for a specific study. Grouping City Object (references other City Objects as members, not a physical object itself). Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Grouping module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: GenericCityObject
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - GenericCityObject
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#GenericCityObject. A City Object that does not correspond to any of the other more specific defined types. Generic / unclassified City Object. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Generic module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: LandUse
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - LandUse
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#LandUse. An area classified by its land use, e.g. residential, industrial, or agricultural. Land use City Object. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 LandUse module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: OtherConstruction
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - OtherConstruction
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#OtherConstruction. A construction that does not fit any of the other defined City Object types. Generic / unclassified City Object. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Generic module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: PlantCover
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - PlantCover
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#PlantCover. An area covered by vegetation of a homogeneous type, e.g. a forest or park lawn (as opposed to a single tree). Vegetation-related City Object. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Vegetation module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: Railway
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - Railway
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#Railway. A railway line, as part of the transportation network. Part of the Transportation family of City Objects (subclass of the schema's shared _AbstractTransportationComplex). Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Transportation module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: Road
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - Road
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#Road. A road, as part of the transportation network. Part of the Transportation family of City Objects (subclass of the schema's shared _AbstractTransportationComplex). Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Transportation module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: SolitaryVegetationObject
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - SolitaryVegetationObject
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#SolitaryVegetationObject. A single, individually modeled vegetation object, e.g. one tree. Vegetation-related City Object. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Vegetation module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: TINRelief
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - TINRelief
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#TINRelief. A Triangulated Irregular Network representing terrain relief; geometry is restricted to a single CompositeSurface (the triangulated mesh). Terrain/relief City Object.

models.name: TransportSquare
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - TransportSquare
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#TransportSquare. A public square that is part of the transportation network, e.g. a plaza connecting several streets. Part of the Transportation family of City Objects (subclass of the schema's shared _AbstractTransportationComplex). Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Transportation module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: Tunnel
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - Tunnel
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#Tunnel. An underground or covered passage, e.g. a road or rail tunnel. Part of the Tunnel family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Tunnel module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: TunnelConstructiveElement
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - TunnelConstructiveElement
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#TunnelConstructiveElement. A structural element of a Tunnel, e.g. a lining segment, modeled as its own City Object. Part of the Tunnel family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Tunnel module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: TunnelFurniture
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - TunnelFurniture
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#TunnelFurniture. An item of fixed equipment/furniture inside a Tunnel, modeled as its own City Object. Part of the Tunnel family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Tunnel module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: TunnelHollowSpace
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - TunnelHollowSpace
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#TunnelHollowSpace. An interior hollow space within a Tunnel. Part of the Tunnel family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Tunnel module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: TunnelInstallation
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - TunnelInstallation
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#TunnelInstallation. A construction attached to a Tunnel that is too small/detailed to be a TunnelPart, e.g. ventilation equipment. Part of the Tunnel family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Tunnel module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: TunnelPart
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - TunnelPart
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#TunnelPart. A self-contained part of a Tunnel with its own geometry and attributes. Must reference its parent Tunnel via `parents`. Part of the Tunnel family of City Objects. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Tunnel module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: WaterBody
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - WaterBody
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#WaterBody. A body of water, e.g. a lake, river, or sea area. Water-related City Object. Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Water module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

models.name: Waterway
models.title: Smart Data Models - CityJSON v2.0 - Waterway
models.description: https://www.cityjson.org/schemas/2.0.2/cityobjects.schema.json#Waterway. A waterway used for transportation (navigable water route). Part of the Transportation family of City Objects (subclass of the schema's shared _AbstractTransportationComplex). Typed attributes cross-referenced from the CityGML 3.0 Transportation module (schemas.opengis.net/citygml/), the data model CityJSON's own attributes are informally derived from.

title: DCSA Track & Trace (Digital Container Shipping Association)
description: DCSA, the association of the major container carriers, publishes open digital standards for container shipping (Track & Trace, Booking, electronic Bill of Lading, Operational Vessel Schedules, Commercial Schedules, Just-in-Time Port Call, ...). Track & Trace defines the events that carriers publish about a container shipment: shipment events (status of a booking or transport document), transport events (arrival and departure of a vessel, barge, rail or truck at a transport call) and equipment events (gate in/out, loading, discharge, stuffing, stripping and inspection of a container). It is offered as a polling and subscription (push) API and is implemented by the major ocean carriers.
publisher: Digital Container Shipping Association (DCSA)

models.name: EquipmentEvent
models.title: Smart Data Models - DCSA Track & Trace - EquipmentEvent
models.description: The equipment event entity is a specialization of the event entity to support specification of data that only applies to an equipment event. (DCSA Track & Trace 2.2.0, OpenAPI component equipmentEvent; field names kept verbatim; deprecated fields left out.)

models.name: ShipmentEvent
models.title: Smart Data Models - DCSA Track & Trace - ShipmentEvent
models.description: The shipment event entity is a specialization of the event entity to support specification of data that only applies to a shipment event. (DCSA Track & Trace 2.2.0, OpenAPI component shipmentEvent; field names kept verbatim; deprecated fields left out.)

models.name: TransportEvent
models.title: Smart Data Models - DCSA Track & Trace - TransportEvent
models.description: The transport event entity is a specialization of the event entity to support specification of data that only applies to a transport event. (DCSA Track & Trace 2.2.0, OpenAPI component transportEvent; field names kept verbatim; deprecated fields left out.)

title: EDINT City Agenda Ontology (Ontología de Agenda Ciudadana)
description: Vocabulary for city events published in municipal public agendas -- cultural, sports and social activities, fairs, exhibitions, concerts -- reusing schema.org's Event for scheduling and GeoSPARQL for location.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: CityEvent
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT City Agenda - CityEvent
models.description: An event that will take place in a city, e.g. a cultural, sports or social activity published in a municipal public agenda (edintagenda:CityEvent, subclass of geosparql:Feature and schema:Event).

title: EDINT Public Lighting Ontology (Ontología de Alumbrado Público)
description: Vocabulary for public street lighting inventory in the context of FEMP (Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces): modular streetlight composition (post, luminaire, lamp, junction box), electrical infrastructure (control center), energy consumption as a SOSA observation with QUDT results, luminaire model catalog, manufacturer, photometric and light-pollution parameters, and conservation status.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: Brazo
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - Brazo
models.description: Arm of the post that supports a luminaire. A post can have multiple arms, each with its own height (edintalu:Brazo).

models.name: Caja
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - Caja
models.description: Junction box or access point for the streetlight's electrical cables. Optional -- not all streetlights have an accessible box (edintalu:Caja).

models.name: CentroDeMando
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - CentroDeMando
models.description: Electrical panel or control center on which one or more streetlights depend (edintalu:CentroDeMando, subclass of edint-suministro's UtilitySupplyPoint) -- the point where electricity reaches the lighting installation.

models.name: ConsumoEnergetico
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - ConsumoEnergetico
models.description: Observation of electricity consumption in a specific tariff period (edintalu:ConsumoEnergetico, subclass of edint-suministro's UtilityConsumption, itself a sosa:Observation). Each instance represents ONE tariff period; the total for a fiscal year is obtained by summing instances of the same period.

models.name: Fabricante
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - Fabricante
models.description: Entity that manufactures street lighting components: posts, luminaires, lamps, boxes or models (edintalu:Fabricante). NOTE: no other class in this ontology version declares a relationship pointing at Fabricante -- it is not referenced by Poste, Luminaria, Lampara, Caja or ModeloLuminaria despite the ontology's own prose describing it as linked to all of them. See standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: Farola
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - Farola
models.description: A complete point of light, composed of a post, one or more luminaires (which in turn contain lamps) and optionally a junction box (edintalu:Farola, subclass of edint-infraestructura's UrbanElement).

models.name: Lampara
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - Lampara
models.description: Light source: bulb, LED module or converter of electrical energy into light. Each luminaire houses exactly one lamp (edintalu:Lampara). Includes photometric properties and rated life.

models.name: Luminaria
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - Luminaria
models.description: Lighting apparatus that houses, directs and filters the light from the lamp. A streetlight can have multiple luminaires, e.g. LED+DISCHARGE (edintalu:Luminaria).

models.name: ModeloLuminaria
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - ModeloLuminaria
models.description: Entry in the luminaire model catalog (edintalu:ModeloLuminaria). NOTE: the source ontology's own prose says this 'allows linking manufacturer, nominal power, technology and photometric specifications', but no such properties are actually declared for this class in this ontology version -- only a generic 'name' applies. See standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: Poste
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - Poste
models.description: Physical support of the streetlight: column, bracket, wall, short post, etc. (edintalu:Poste). The specific type is indicated via tipoSoporte.

models.name: ReductorFlujo
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - ReductorFlujo
models.description: Energy saving system that reduces luminous flux, located either in the luminaire (lamp regulator) or at the start of the installation (head-end regulator) (edintalu:ReductorFlujo). NOTE: like Fabricante, no other class declares a relationship pointing at ReductorFlujo in this ontology version -- see standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: SuministroElectrico
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Lighting - SuministroElectrico
models.description: Electricity supply contract associated with a control center, including tariff, voltage, and consumption by tariff periods (edintalu:SuministroElectrico, subclass of edint-suministro's UtilityContract).

title: EDINT Parking Ontology (Ontología de Aparcamiento)
description: Vocabulary for representing a municipality's public and private parking -- on-street and off-street -- including access points (linked to edint-infraestructura's sensor representation), fees, individual spots, and spot groupings by permit type or vehicle type. The source ontology explicitly states that Parking is a specialization of edint-infraestructura's Facility.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: Parking
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Parking - Parking
models.description: Parking for different types of vehicles, on-street or off-street, public or private (edintapar:Parking, subclass of edintinf:Facility). Collapses the source ontology's two concrete subclasses (OnStreetParking, OffStreetParking) into a single entity with a parkingType discriminator, since the source's own real example data never instantiates bare Parking directly and OnStreetParking's only distinguishing property (isPartOfZone) is small enough to keep as an always-optional field rather than a second entity type.

models.name: ParkingFee
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Parking - ParkingFee
models.description: Parking fee that covers the right to park a vehicle in an authorized space for a certain time period (edintapar:ParkingFee). The source ontology defines no properties of its own; it is the target of Parking.hasParkingFee.

models.name: ParkingSpot
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Parking - ParkingSpot
models.description: Individual parking spot in an on-street or off-street parking (edintapar:ParkingSpot). The source ontology defines no properties of its own; it is the target of Parking/ParkingSpotsByPermitType/ParkingSpotsByVehicleType's hasParkingSpot relationship.

models.name: ParkingSpotsByPermitType
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Parking - ParkingSpotsByPermitType
models.description: Group of parking spots for each type of permit, e.g. resident, rotation (edintapar:ParkingSpotsByPermitType). Indicates the number of slots for that permit type. NOTE: the source ontology's own 'permitType' property declares rdfs:domain :ParkingSpotsByVehicleType (not ParkingSpotsByPermitType) -- almost certainly a copy-paste error in the source, given the property's own name and comment ('Relationship between the group of places by TYPE OF PERMIT and the taxonomy of types of permit'). Assigned to this entity instead, per the property's evident intent; see standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: ParkingSpotsByVehicleType
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Parking - ParkingSpotsByVehicleType
models.description: Group of parking spots for each type of vehicle: cars, motorcycles, bicycles, among others (edintapar:ParkingSpotsByVehicleType). Indicates the number of slots per vehicle type. NOTE: the source ontology declares no rdfs:domain at all for its 'vehicleType' property; assigned to this entity per the property's own name/comment (mirroring the equally-evident, but differently-broken, permitType situation on ParkingSpotsByPermitType); see standard-metadata.yaml.

title: EDINT Spanish Cadastre Ontology (Ontología del Catastro Inmobiliario Español)
description: Vocabulary for the Spanish Real Estate Cadastre (Catastro Inmobiliario): cadastral parcels, properties, constructions, their references, and renovation events. Scope explicitly excludes ownership, valuation, transmission data and administrative processes (per the source's own stated scope).
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: CadastralConstruction
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Catastro - CadastralConstruction
models.description: Building or construction registered on a cadastral property: area, use, construction characteristics, and renovations (edintcat:CadastralConstruction, subclass of geosparql:Feature). Located on exactly one cadastral property.

models.name: CadastralParcel
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Catastro - CadastralParcel
models.description: Basic unit of territorial division in the Spanish Cadastre: a plot of land delimited geographically, which may contain one or more cadastral properties (edintcat:CadastralParcel, subclass of geosparql:Feature).

models.name: CadastralProperty
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Catastro - CadastralProperty
models.description: Real estate property registered in the Cadastre: a premises, dwelling, or any independent use unit within a parcel (edintcat:CadastralProperty, subclass of geosparql:Feature). A cadastral property may have one or more constructions associated.

models.name: ParcelReference
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Catastro - ParcelReference
models.description: Reference identifying a cadastral parcel: a 7-character alphanumeric code (edintcat:ParcelReference, subclass of the abstract edintcat:CadastralReference).

models.name: PropertyReference
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Catastro - PropertyReference
models.description: Reference identifying a cadastral property: the parcel reference plus the property reference with check digit, e.g. TF8006N0001HZ (edintcat:PropertyReference, subclass of the abstract edintcat:CadastralReference).

models.name: Renovation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Catastro - Renovation
models.description: Event or process of renovating a construction: when it occurred and what type of renovation was performed (edintcat:Renovation).

title: EDINT Commercial Premises Census Ontology (Ontología de Censo de Locales Comerciales)
description: Vocabulary for a municipality's commercial premises census: commercial spaces (shops, offices), the entities/organizations that operate in them, their operating permits, associated terraces, and commercial aggregations such as shopping centers or traditional markets.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: CommercialAggregation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Commercial Census - CommercialAggregation
models.description: The integration of several establishments or points of sale in the same physical space, such as a shopping center or a traditional market (edintcom:CommercialAggregation, subclass of edint-infraestructura's Facility). NOTE: the source ontology's own ontology.ttl redeclares 'Facility' (and InfrastructureElement/UrbanElement) under this ontology's OWN censo-locales# namespace, rather than importing/reusing edint-infraestructura's real classes -- almost certainly an artifact of copying a template ontology, not an intentional new class; this candidate treats these subclass relationships as targeting edint-infraestructura's real Facility, not the namespace-duplicate one. See standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: CommercialEntity
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Commercial Census - CommercialEntity
models.description: A person and/or organization that carries out an economic activity and is assigned the permit of a commercial space (edintcom:CommercialEntity).

models.name: CommercialSpace
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Commercial Census - CommercialSpace
models.description: A physical place prepared for selling products, providing services, or serving customers, such as a shop, premises or office (edintcom:CommercialSpace, subclass of edint-infraestructura's Facility).

models.name: Permit
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Commercial Census - Permit
models.description: The license/authorization of a commercial space, terrace or economic activity (edintcom:Permit). NOTE: unrelated to, and a distinct concept from, edint-censo-vehiculos's own 'Permit' entity (vehicle circulation/parking permits) -- same entity type NAME, entirely different meaning; a genuine type collision, not resolved here. See standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: Terrace
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Commercial Census - Terrace
models.description: An open area connected to a bar, restaurant, etc., serving as an outdoor sitting area for clients (edintcom:Terrace, subclass of edint-infraestructura's Facility).

title: EDINT Vehicle Census Ontology (Ontología de Censo/Registro de Vehículos)
description: Vocabulary for representing the vehicle census/registry that local entities manage for purposes such as vehicle tax collection (IVTM in Spain) and mobility management (parking permits, zone access permits). Scope is limited to data usable for those two purposes; driving-licence, technical inspection and similar vehicle data are explicitly out of scope per the source ontology's own stated purpose. Reuses SAREF4AUTO (vehicle), schema.org (Person/Organization) and SKOS (controlled vocabularies).
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: Permit
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Vehicle Census - Permit
models.description: Official permit, usually issued by the city council or the traffic authority, that allows a particular vehicle to access, drive through, or park in an area where entry is restricted or regulated (edintveh:Permit).

models.name: Vehicle
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Vehicle Census - Vehicle
models.description: A vehicle registered in a local entity's vehicle census/registry, used for purposes such as vehicle tax collection or mobility management (edintveh:Vehicle, reusing SAREF4AUTO's saref4auto:Vehicle).

title: EDINT Noise Pollution Ontology (Ontología de Contaminación Acústica)
description: Small domain extension of the EDINT Environmental Sensors Ontology (edint-medio-ambiente) for noise pollution observations, adding acoustic-measurement-specific properties (frequency weighting, time constant, reference interval, level statistic, predominant emitter type).
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: NoiseObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Noise Pollution - NoiseObservation
models.description: An observation of a noise property made by a noise sensor (edintacus:NoiseObservation, subclass of edint-medio-ambiente's EnvironmentalObservation). Small domain extension adding acoustic-measurement-specific properties on top of the base EnvironmentalObservation pattern.

title: EDINT Photovoltaic System Ontology (Ontología de Instalación Fotovoltaica)
description: Vocabulary for representing photovoltaic (solar) installations found on a municipality's infrastructure elements, and the measurement of electricity generation, consumption, accumulation and grid export from those installations. Reuses SOSA/SSN (sensors and observations), SAREF (Meter), GeoSPARQL (geometry) and schema.org (Organization).
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: PhotovoltaicGeneration
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Photovoltaic - PhotovoltaicGeneration
models.description: Amount of electricity generated, consumed, stored or exported by a photovoltaic system during a certain period of time (edintfotov:PhotovoltaicGeneration, subclass of sosa:Observation). Which of generation/consumption/storage/export a given observation represents is expected to be conveyed via observedProperty's target concept -- the source ontology does not declare a dedicated categorization property or controlled vocabulary for this distinction.

models.name: PhotovoltaicMeter
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Photovoltaic - PhotovoltaicMeter
models.description: Device that measures and records the total electricity produced, consumed, stored and exported by a photovoltaic system, in real-time and cumulatively (edintfotov:PhotovoltaicMeter, subclass of sosa:Sensor and saref:Meter).

models.name: PhotovoltaicSystem
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Photovoltaic - PhotovoltaicSystem
models.description: A photovoltaic (PV) system that converts sunlight into electricity, installed on a municipal infrastructure element (edintfotov:PhotovoltaicSystem, subclass of geosparql:Feature and sosa:FeatureOfInterest). Ranges from residential rooftops to utility-scale plants.

models.name: PhotovoltaicSystemContract
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Photovoltaic - PhotovoltaicSystemContract
models.description: Legally binding document outlining the sale, lease, or power purchase agreement for solar panels (edintfotov:PhotovoltaicSystemContract).

models.name: PhotovoltaicSystemRate
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Photovoltaic - PhotovoltaicSystemRate
models.description: Policy mechanism that pays solar system owners for the surplus electricity they generate and feed back into the national grid (edintfotov:PhotovoltaicSystemRate). The source ontology defines no properties of its own; it is the target of PhotovoltaicSystemContract.hasRate.

title: EDINT Waste Management Ontology (Ontología de Gestión de Residuos)
description: Vocabulary for municipal waste management infrastructure: mobile and permanent collection points ("puntos limpios"), street waste containers, and authorized waste management/treatment facilities.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: MobileCollectionPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Waste Management - MobileCollectionPoint
models.description: A temporary, mobile waste collection point, e.g. a scheduled collection van visiting a street on a set day/time (edintwaste:MobileCollectionPoint, subclass of edintwaste:CollectionPoint, edintwaste:WasteFacility, edint-infraestructura's Facility). Bare CollectionPoint/WasteFacility are not materialized as their own entities, matching this candidate family's precedent for abstract bases.

models.name: PermanentCollectionPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Waste Management - PermanentCollectionPoint
models.description: A permanent, fixed waste collection point, e.g. a 'punto limpio' civic amenity site (edintwaste:PermanentCollectionPoint, subclass of edintwaste:CollectionPoint, edintwaste:WasteFacility, edint-infraestructura's Facility). No properties of its own beyond those inherited from CollectionPoint.

models.name: WasteContainer
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Waste Management - WasteContainer
models.description: A street waste container, e.g. for glass, plastics/metals/cartons, or general waste (edintwaste:WasteContainer, subclass of edintwaste:WasteFacility, edint-infraestructura's Facility).

models.name: WasteManagementFacility
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Waste Management - WasteManagementFacility
models.description: A facility authorized to manage/treat waste, e.g. a classification or treatment plant (edintwaste:WasteManagementFacility, subclass of edintwaste:WasteFacility, edint-infraestructura's Facility).

title: EDINT Infrastructure Ontology (Ontología de Infraestructura)
description: Vocabulary for representing a municipality's public and private infrastructure facilities (educational, cultural, social, sports and health centers, on-street and off-street parking, shared-bicycle stations) together with the sensors, observations, violations, management roles and organizations involved in operating and monitoring them, plus (as of this update) street sections, traffic incidences, traffic control/measuring equipment and observations, and regulated zones. Reuses SOSA/SSN (sensors and observations), GeoSPARQL (geometry), W3C Time, QUDT, schema.org and Dublin Core.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) as technical developer

models.name: AccessObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - AccessObservation
models.description: Observation carried out at any entrance to a municipal facility. This includes pedestrian or vehicle access (edintinf:AccessObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: AccessSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - AccessSensor
models.description: A device that records the access of people or vehicles. This could be an LPR (license plate recognition) camera, a building entrance door sensor, or other similar devices (edintinf:AccessSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor).

models.name: BikeSharingStation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - BikeSharingStation
models.description: A Facility specialization for shared-bicycle stations (edintinf:EstacionBicicleta). Like Parking, the source ontology defines no attributes of its own beyond those inherited from Facility. Check for overlap with any existing bike-sharing SDM model before promoting this candidate.

models.name: CadastralProperty
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - CadastralProperty
models.description: Real estate property registered in the Cadastre (catastro:CadastralProperty). Can be a premises, dwelling, or any independent use unit within a parcel; a cadastral property may have one or more constructions associated. The source ontology defines no attributes of its own; it is the target of the Facility.isCadastralProperty relationship, added in ontology v0.2.1.

models.name: CountingObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - CountingObservation
models.description: Observation on the number of people or vehicles that a sensor counts (edintinf:CountingObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: CountingSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - CountingSensor
models.description: A device that records the number of people or vehicles that it observes (edintinf:CountingSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor).

models.name: Facility
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Facility
models.description: It refers to service buildings (public or private), leisure areas, commercial areas or any other element that directly affects mobility, acting as a focus of attraction for persons or vehicles. Source: EDINT Infrastructure Ontology (edintinf:Facility).

models.name: ManagementRole
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - ManagementRole
models.description: The role that the municipal administration or one of its departments plays in the management of a municipal facility. This may include ownership, maintenance, security, among others (edintinf:ManagementRole).

models.name: ObservationPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - ObservationPoint
models.description: Points where access or counting observations can be made using sensors (edintinf:ObservationPoint). The source ontology defines no attributes of its own beyond location; it is the target of the Facility.hasObservationPoint relationship.

models.name: Organization
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Organization
models.description: Any public or private organization that owns or manages an element of the infrastructure (edintinf:Organization). NOTE: check for overlap with the existing official Smart Data Models 'dataModel.Organization' subject before promoting this candidate.

models.name: Parking
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Parking
models.description: A Facility specialization for on-street and off-street parking areas. The source ontology (edintinf:Parking) defines no attributes beyond those inherited from Facility; it is distinguished only by its NGSI-LD type and, typically, its infrastructureType value. NOTE: this concept is likely to overlap with the already-existing official Smart Data Models 'dataModel.Parking' subject (e.g. OffStreetParking/OnStreetParking) — check for duplication before promoting this candidate.

models.name: PlannedIncidence
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - PlannedIncidence
models.description: Planned traffic incidence, can be recurrent or not (edinttrafico:PlannedIncidence, subclass of edinttrafico:Incidence and geosparql:Feature). Carries Incidence's own base properties (incidenceInSection, incidenceType, startDate, endDate, incidenceAttachment, numDirections) plus its own (expectedEndDate, isRecurrent, recurrence). Formerly excluded as part of an external-ontology traffic branch; now natively defined as of source ontology v0.2.1.

models.name: RegulatedZone
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - RegulatedZone
models.description: Area to which a particular regulation or policy applies (zone:RegulatedZone), e.g. a low-emissions zone or a residents-only parking area. The source ontology defines no attributes of its own; it is the target of the Facility.locatedInZone relationship, added in ontology v0.2.1.

models.name: StreetSection
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - StreetSection
models.description: Section defined by a starting and an ending point that can belong to one or more street (edinttrafico:StreetSection, subclass of geosparql:Feature). Formerly modeled in an external ontology (ciudadesabiertas.es) and excluded from this candidate's first translation pass; now natively defined in the source repository's own trafico# sub-vocabulary as of ontology v0.2.1, so brought into scope.

models.name: TrafficEquipment
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - TrafficEquipment
models.description: A traffic equipment monitors or controls the traffic of a city, e.g. a traffic light or control equipment that is not a measuring device (edinttrafico:TrafficEquipment, subclass of geosparql:Feature). TrafficMeasuringDevice is a concrete subclass for equipment that also performs measurements; this entity covers equipment that does not. Formerly excluded as part of an external-ontology traffic branch; now natively defined as of source ontology v0.2.1.

models.name: TrafficMeasuringDevice
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - TrafficMeasuringDevice
models.description: Traffic measuring device, a type of traffic equipment which performs measurements, e.g. a speed radar or an Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system (edinttrafico:TrafficMeasuringDevice, subclass of sosa:Sensor, edinttrafico:TrafficEquipment and geosparql:Feature). Combines TrafficEquipment's own properties (monitors, trafficEquipmentType, numDirections, urban) with Sensor's (observableProperty) and its own (manufacturer, inService, measurementFrequency). Formerly excluded as part of an external-ontology traffic branch; now natively defined as of source ontology v0.2.1.

models.name: TrafficObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - TrafficObservation
models.description: Observation by a traffic measuring device or a control equipment such as speed cameras or Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) systems (edinttrafico:TrafficObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation). Follows the same SOSA Observation pattern already used by this candidate's CountingObservation/AccessObservation, plus its own 'validated' property. Formerly excluded as part of an external-ontology traffic branch; now natively defined as of source ontology v0.2.1.

models.name: UnplannedIncidence
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - UnplannedIncidence
models.description: Unplanned traffic incidence in a city (edinttrafico:UnplannedIncidence, subclass of edinttrafico:Incidence and geosparql:Feature). The source ontology defines no properties of its own beyond those inherited from Incidence (incidenceInSection, incidenceType, startDate, endDate, incidenceAttachment, numDirections). Formerly excluded as part of an external-ontology traffic branch; now natively defined as of source ontology v0.2.1.

models.name: Violation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Violation
models.description: Non-compliance or violation of traffic or access rules, road laws or local ordinances by a person or a driver or owner of a vehicle (edintinf:Violation).

title: EDINT Environmental Sensors Ontology (Ontología de Sensores Medioambientales)
description: Generic vocabulary for environmental sensor platforms, sensors and observations -- a lightweight, modular extension of SOSA (Sensor, Observation, Sample, and Actuator) and GeoSPARQL, restricting its measurements to EDINT's own controlled vocabularies. Designed to be specialized per environmental domain (air quality, climatology, noise pollution) purely through those vocabularies, without new subclasses.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: EnvironmentalObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Environmental Sensors - EnvironmentalObservation
models.description: An observation of an environmental property made by an environmental sensor (edintmed:EnvironmentalObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: EnvironmentalSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Environmental Sensors - EnvironmentalSensor
models.description: Device designed to observe and measure physical, chemical, or acoustic properties of the environment (edintmed:EnvironmentalSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor). This ontology is deliberately generic: domain specializations (air quality, climatology, noise pollution) reuse it as-is, specializing only through the open controlled-vocabulary Relationships below rather than through new subclasses.

models.name: SensorPlatform
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Environmental Sensors - SensorPlatform
models.description: Physical platform or facility that hosts environmental sensors for monitoring, e.g. an air-quality cabin, a water buoy, or a weather tower (edintmed:SensorPlatform, subclass of geosparql:Feature and sosa:Platform).

title: EDINT Real Estate Offer Ontology (Ontología de Oferta Inmobiliaria)
description: Vocabulary for real estate listings/offers -- sale, rent, or transfer of a property -- referencing the corresponding cadastral parcel or property.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: RealEstateListing
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Real Estate Offer - RealEstateListing
models.description: A real estate listing representing an offer for a property -- sale, rent, or transfer (edintinm:RealEstateListing). NOTE: the source ontology's own generated ontology.ttl declares this class as subClassOf a class named 'Error1' in an 'org.semanticweb.owlapi/error#' namespace -- an OWL-API tooling artifact from a malformed-axiom placeholder, not a real superclass. Ignored here; not modeled as any kind of inheritance.

title: EDINT Public Organizations Ontology (Ontología de Organizaciones Públicas)
description: Vocabulary for representing Spanish public administration organizations and their place in an organization chart. An adaptation of the W3C Organization Ontology for EDINT's requirements.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: Organization
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Organizations - Organization
models.description: A public administration organization in Spain, and its place in an organization chart (edintorg:Organization, subclass of W3C org:Organization). Collapses the source ontology's two subclasses (OrganicUnit, PublicLawEntity), which declare no properties of their own, into this single entity -- the hasOrganizationType enum below already captures similar distinctions in practice.

title: EDINT Commercial Promotion Ontology (Ontología de Promoción Comercial)
description: Vocabulary for commercial promotion: campaigns (vouchers, discounts, revitalization drives) and events (fairs, thematic markets, local events) run to promote commercial activity in a zone.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: CommercialCampaign
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Commercial Promotion - CommercialCampaign
models.description: A commercial promotion campaign, e.g. a voucher or discount campaign run across several commercial spaces (edintpro:CommercialCampaign). This ontology's own CommercialSpace declaration is a pointer (rdfs:isDefinedBy) to edint-censo-locales's real CommercialSpace, not a separate definition; not re-modeled here.

models.name: CommercialEvent
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Commercial Promotion - CommercialEvent
models.description: A commercial promotion event, e.g. a fair or thematic market (edintpro:CommercialEvent, subclass of schema:Event).

title: EDINT Public Services Ontology (Ontología de Servicios Públicos)
description: Vocabulary for municipal public services and the administrative procedures through which they are managed and resolved, reusing the EU's Core Public Service Vocabulary (CPSV-AP) for competent authorities, contact points and channels.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: AdministrativeProcedure
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Services - AdministrativeProcedure
models.description: Formal process followed by a public administration to manage, evaluate, and resolve a request, case, or administrative action (edintserpub:AdministrativeProcedure). NOTE: same tooling artifact as PublicService -- the source ontology's own class declaration uses a malformed IRI (owlapi/turtle# namespace); this entity uses the real servicios-publicos# IRI confirmed by the property domains and the source's own real example data.

models.name: PublicService
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Public Services - PublicService
models.description: A municipal public service offered by a public administration or by an entity on its behalf (edintserpub:PublicService). NOTE: the source ontology's own generated ontology.ttl has two tooling artifacts affecting this class: its own class IRI is malformed (declared under 'http://www.semanticweb.org/owl/owlapi/turtle#' instead of this ontology's real servicios-publicos# namespace), and it is declared rdfs:subClassOf itself (a tautology). Both ignored here; this entity uses the real servicios-publicos# IRI confirmed by the property domains and the source's own real example data.

title: EDINT Utility Supply Ontology (Ontología de Suministro)
description: Vocabulary for utilities (electricity, gas, water, ...) supplied to a municipality's infrastructure elements, and the measurement of their consumption. Structurally near-identical to edint-fotovoltaica (System/Meter/Generation/Contract/Rate), applied to utility supply generally rather than photovoltaic generation specifically.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: UtilityConsumption
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Utility Supply - UtilityConsumption
models.description: Amount of a utility (electricity, gas, water, ...) consumed over a specific period (edintsum:UtilityConsumption, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: UtilityContract
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Utility Supply - UtilityContract
models.description: Agreement between a utility provider and a consumer defining the terms, rates, service quality, and responsibilities for providing a utility like electricity, water, or gas (edintsum:UtilityContract).

models.name: UtilityMeter
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Utility Supply - UtilityMeter
models.description: Device that measures the consumption of a utility, e.g. electricity, gas, water, or heating (edintsum:UtilityMeter, subclass of sosa:Sensor and saref:Meter).

models.name: UtilityRate
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Utility Supply - UtilityRate
models.description: The rate/tariff applied in a utility contract (edintsum:UtilityRate). The source ontology defines no properties of its own; it is the target of UtilityContract.hasRate.

models.name: UtilitySupplyPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Utility Supply - UtilitySupplyPoint
models.description: Point of a municipal infrastructure element where a utility (electricity, gas, water, ...) is supplied, generally associated with a UtilityMeter (edintsum:UtilitySupplyPoint, subclass of geosparql:Feature and sosa:FeatureOfInterest).

title: EDINT Traffic Ontology (Ontología de Tráfico)
description: Vocabulary for street sections, traffic incidents (planned and unplanned), traffic control and measuring equipment, traffic observations, and traffic observation points.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: ControlEquipment
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Traffic - ControlEquipment
models.description: Equipment that monitors or controls properties of a specific vehicle, such as its speed or access to certain city areas -- e.g. a traffic light or speed/access control camera (edinttrafico:ControlEquipment, subclass of edinttrafico:TrafficEquipment). This is a NEW concrete subclass introduced in this standalone ontology (v0.1.1) that did not exist when edint-infraestructura's own v0.2.1 update bundled an earlier copy of this pattern -- that earlier copy materialized bare 'TrafficEquipment' directly for this same purpose. See standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: PlannedIncident
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Traffic - PlannedIncident
models.description: Planned traffic incident, can be recurrent or not (edinttrafico:PlannedIncident, subclass of edinttrafico:Incident and geosparql:Feature). Bare 'Incident' is deliberately not materialized as its own entity, matching this candidate family's precedent for abstract SOSA-style bases (e.g. Sensor). Renamed from 'Incidence'/'PlannedIncidence' used in edint-infraestructura's own bundled v0.2.1 copy of this pattern -- see standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: StreetSection
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Traffic - StreetSection
models.description: Section defined by a starting and an ending point that can belong to one or more street (edinttrafico:StreetSection, subclass of geosparql:Feature). Translated from the dedicated, standalone edint-ontologia-trafico repository (v0.1.1) -- more current than, and using slightly different naming from, the same-purpose entities bundled inline into edint-infraestructura's own v0.2.1 update; see standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: TrafficMeasurementDevice
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Traffic - TrafficMeasurementDevice
models.description: Traffic measurement device, a type of traffic equipment which performs measurements of properties such as service level, traffic intensity and traffic load (edinttrafico:TrafficMeasurementDevice, subclass of sosa:Sensor and edinttrafico:TrafficEquipment). Renamed from 'TrafficMeasuringDevice' used in edint-infraestructura's own bundled v0.2.1 copy; NOTE this newer version no longer carries numDirections/urban (moved exclusively to the new ControlEquipment sibling) -- see standard-metadata.yaml.

models.name: TrafficObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Traffic - TrafficObservation
models.description: Observation by a traffic measurement device or a control equipment such as speed cameras or Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) systems (edinttrafico:TrafficObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: TrafficObservationPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Traffic - TrafficObservationPoint
models.description: Point where traffic or specific-vehicle observations can be made using sensors (edinttrafico:TrafficObservationPoint, subclass of sosa:FeatureOfInterest). No properties of its own beyond location; parallels edint-infraestructura's ObservationPoint, but specific to the traffic domain -- a new class not present in the earlier copy of this pattern bundled into edint-infraestructura's v0.2.1 update.

models.name: UnplannedIncident
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Traffic - UnplannedIncident
models.description: Unplanned traffic incident in a city (edinttrafico:UnplannedIncident, subclass of edinttrafico:Incident and geosparql:Feature). No properties of its own beyond those inherited from Incident.

title: SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology, as demonstrated by the EDINT Tourism repository
description: Vocabulary for representing tourism accommodation establishments (hotels, guest houses, aparthotels) and historical/cultural resources (fortified palaces, amphitheatres, aqueducts, and 40+ related types), together with their location, contact points, booking channels, ratings and descriptions. Drawn from SEGITTUR's Core Tourism Ontology (estur:), a large (388-class) reference model for a Network of Tourism Sector Ontologies serving Spain's future Intelligent Destination Platform (PID).
publisher: SEGITTUR (Sociedad Estatal para la Gestión de la Innovación y las Tecnologías Turísticas), with the Ontology Engineering Group (Universidad Politécnica de Madrid), Globaldit and Gnoss as technical developers

models.name: Alcazar
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Alcazar
models.description: Alcazar (fortified palace), a specialization of HistoricalOrCulturalResource (estur:HistoricalOrCulturalResource, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology) — one of 43 such subclasses in the full ontology (others include Museum, Castle, Cathedral, Monastery, etc.), of which this candidate only covers the three demonstrated with real example data. NOTE: the source repository's example data uses the misspellings 'Amphiteatre' and 'Acueduct'; the authoritative ontology spells these 'Amphitheatre' and 'Aqueduct', which are used here.

models.name: Amphitheatre
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Amphitheatre
models.description: Amphitheatre, a specialization of HistoricalOrCulturalResource (estur:HistoricalOrCulturalResource, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology) — one of 43 such subclasses in the full ontology (others include Museum, Castle, Cathedral, Monastery, etc.), of which this candidate only covers the three demonstrated with real example data. NOTE: the source repository's example data uses the misspellings 'Amphiteatre' and 'Acueduct'; the authoritative ontology spells these 'Amphitheatre' and 'Aqueduct', which are used here.

models.name: Aparthotel
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Aparthotel
models.description: Aparthotel, a specialization of AccommodationEstablishment (estur:AccommodationEstablishment via TourismOrRelatedFacility, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source repository's README uses the misspelling 'AccomodationEstablishment' (single 'm'); the authoritative ontology spells it 'AccommodationEstablishment' (double 'm'), which is used throughout this candidate.

models.name: Aqueduct
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Aqueduct
models.description: Aqueduct, a specialization of HistoricalOrCulturalResource (estur:HistoricalOrCulturalResource, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology) — one of 43 such subclasses in the full ontology (others include Museum, Castle, Cathedral, Monastery, etc.), of which this candidate only covers the three demonstrated with real example data. NOTE: the source repository's example data uses the misspellings 'Amphiteatre' and 'Acueduct'; the authoritative ontology spells these 'Amphitheatre' and 'Aqueduct', which are used here.

models.name: BookingChannel
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - BookingChannel
models.description: A channel through which a tourism resource, service or organisation can be booked (estur:BookingChannel, a ContactPoint subclass, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: ContactPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - ContactPoint
models.description: A means of contacting a tourism entity or organisation (estur:ContactPoint, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: Description
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Description
models.description: A textual description of a tourism entity (estur:Description, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: Hostal
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Hostal
models.description: Hostal (Spanish guest house), a specialization of AccommodationEstablishment (estur:AccommodationEstablishment via TourismOrRelatedFacility, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source repository's README uses the misspelling 'AccomodationEstablishment' (single 'm'); the authoritative ontology spells it 'AccommodationEstablishment' (double 'm'), which is used throughout this candidate.

models.name: Hotel
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Hotel
models.description: Hotel, a specialization of AccommodationEstablishment (estur:AccommodationEstablishment via TourismOrRelatedFacility, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source repository's README uses the misspelling 'AccomodationEstablishment' (single 'm'); the authoritative ontology spells it 'AccommodationEstablishment' (double 'm'), which is used throughout this candidate.

models.name: Location
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Location
models.description: The location of a tourism entity (accommodation, historical/cultural resource, etc.), modeled as a standalone, referenceable resource, matching the source ontology's own design (estur:Location, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology).

models.name: Rating
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Tourism - Rating
models.description: A rating of a tourism resource, service or organisation (estur:Rating, SEGITTUR Core Tourism Ontology). NOTE: the source ontology's own SHACL shapes define a different, incompatible field set for Rating (bookingValue/googleReviewValue/tripAdvisorValue as floats, plus a flat 'stars' integer directly on Hotel) that does not match either the OWL property definitions or any real example data found. This candidate follows ratingUnit/ratingValue because that is what the real, published open-data examples (and the OWL definitions) actually use — check with SEGITTUR before assuming either naming scheme is final.

title: EDINT Shared Vehicles Ontology (Ontología de Vehículos Compartidos)
description: Vocabulary for shared-mobility vehicles (bikes, e-scooters, cars), their stations and docks, routes and waypoints -- a specialization of edint-censo-vehiculos's Vehicle and edint-infraestructura's Facility.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM/OEG) as technical developer

models.name: Dock
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Shared Vehicles - Dock
models.description: Place in the station where the vehicles are secured (edintvc:Dock, subclass of sosa:FeatureOfInterest).

models.name: DockObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Shared Vehicles - DockObservation
models.description: Observation by a dock sensor that detects the dock's availability -- free to park a vehicle, or occupied (edintvc:DockObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: DockSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Shared Vehicles - DockSensor
models.description: Equipment that allows detecting if a dock is free or occupied (edintvc:DockSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor).

models.name: Route
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Shared Vehicles - Route
models.description: The path traveled to get from an origin to a destination, for a shared vehicle trip (edintvc:Route).

models.name: SharedVehicle
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Shared Vehicles - SharedVehicle
models.description: A transport mode -- car, bike, or e-scooter -- that allows multiple users short-term, on-demand access (edintvc:SharedVehicle, subclass of edint-censo-vehiculos's Vehicle). Inherits Vehicle's full property set (licensePlateNumber, registeredOwner, vehicleType, propulsionType, environmentalBadge) plus its own vehicleState and propulsionSystemType.

models.name: SharedVehicleStation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Shared Vehicles - SharedVehicleStation
